speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing, particularly during certain activities. To begin my examination, can you describe exactly what these episodes look like and at what times they occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is interesting; the combination of stridor worsening with neck flexion and crying, along with vomiting during feeding, suggests a possible vascular ring or laryngomalacia. Can you tell me if you have noticed any difficulty breathing at rest or if there are specific sounds in his throat when he is calm?

REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Flexion_XRay, Laryngoscopy

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pulmonary Artery Slings (Vascular Ring) causing extrinsic tracheal compression, likely confirmed by the characteristic relief with neck extension and recurrent feeding/vomiting episodes.
